evidence: CancelOrderUseCase.ts execute() returns inline literal { id: order.id, status: order.getStatus(), lines: order.lines, createdAt: order.createdAt.toISOString() }
ListOrdersByStatusUseCase.ts execute() maps orders with the same inline OrderDto literal
PlaceOrderUseCase.ts declares private mapToDto(order: Order): OrderDto with the same mapping, which the other use cases don't use
UpdateOrderStatusUseCase.ts execute() returns the same inline OrderDto literal

UpdateOrderStatusUseCase.ts hard-codes const validStatuses: OrderStatus[] = ['placed','paid','packed','shipped','delivered'], repeating the domain's OrderStatus definition and the checks in order.transitionTo
CancelOrderUseCase.ts calls stockManager.releaseStock(products, order) after order.canBeCancelled() but never changes the order's status or calls orderRepository.save
parsedVerdict.reasoning: All five files cover one concern: the application use cases for orders and stock. Each one reads data through the domain repositories and returns DTOs from ../dtos/OrderDto. Two problems break the rubric. First, four use cases each build the same OrderDto object literal ({id, status: getStatus(), lines, createdAt.toISOString()}). Only PlaceOrderUseCase puts this in a helper (a private mapToDto), and the other files don't use it, so a change to OrderDto has to be made in four places. Second, UpdateOrderStatusUseCase has its own hard-coded validStatuses array. That repeats the OrderStatus definition the domain already owns, and status changes go through order.transitionTo, so the status rule now exists in two places. This array also leaves out any 'cancelled' status, which suggests it has already drifted from the domain. A smaller problem: CancelOrderUseCase releases stock but never changes the order's status or saves the order. Lifecycle rules are handled differently across the use cases.

violations.message: Copies the Order-to-OrderDto mapping inline instead of sharing one mapper. It also releases stock without changing the order's status or saving the order, unlike the other order-changing use cases.
